chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Salim the freedman of Tarbal, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him say: 'The world is cycles (of gain and loss). Whatever is yours in it comes to you despite your weakness, and whatever is against you in it comes to you and you cannot resist it with strength.' Then he followed this statement by saying: 'Whoever despairs of what has passed away relieves his body, and whoever is content with what he has been given finds peace in his eyes.'

key_terms.قَرَّتْ عَيْنُهُ: His eye cooled (idiom for finding peace/joy)
key_terms.قَنَعَ: To be content, to be satisfied

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'The world is cycles' in Shia hadith and how does one find peace according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the transient nature of worldly life (dunya) as fluctuating cycles where gains arrive despite human weakness and losses occur despite human strength. He prescribes a dual spiritual remedy: 'despairing' of what is lost to free the body from anxiety, and 'contentment' with what is possessed to quiet the eye, reflecting the Shia emphasis on inner tranquility through detachment from the ephemeral. This teaching underscores the practical application of tawakkul and qana'ah in navigating the inevitable ups and downs of worldly existence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-133 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Muhammad ibn al-Hussein ibn Abil Khat’tab, on the authority of Ali ibn Asbat, on the authority of Salim - the servant of Tarbal that he had heard Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) say,

“The world is making progress. Whatever you earn in this world, you earn it despite your weaknesses. Yet, you may lose some thing and not be able to hold on to them with all your strength.”He (MGB) then added, “Whoever forgets about what he has lost is in comfort, and whoever is pleased with what he has been granted will be cheerful.”
